12: ### Minimality conjecture
13: 
14: For a type-\(A_{n-1}\) bigrassmannian permutation \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), Theorem 5.4 supplies two generating sets for the ideal \(J_v\). The authors conjecture:
15: 
16: > **Conjecture.** The two generating sets for the ideal \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) given in Theorem 5.4 are both minimal.

claims.text: Assume the standard box model \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), \(q=n-r\), and \(J_v=\bigoplus_{\mu\supseteq i^j}\mathbb Zs_\mu\). If \(i=1\), put \(a=\min(q-1,r-j)\). Then \[ J_v/A_+J_v\cong\bigoplus_{t=0}^{a}\mathbb Z\,\overline e_{j+t}. \] Consequently both families \[ \{s_{(t+1,1^{j-1})}:0\le t\le a\},\qquad \{s_{(1^{j+t})}:0\le t\le a\} \] map to integral bases and are irredundant generators of \(J_v\).

If \(j=1\), put \(a=\min(q-i,r-1)\). Then \[ J_v/A_+J_v\cong\bigoplus_{t=0}^{a}\mathbb Z\,\overline h_{i+t}, \] and both families \[ \{s_{(i+t)}:0\le t\le a\},\qquad \{s_{(i,1^t)}:0\le t\le a\} \] map to integral bases and are irredundant.
